# Rule files

These rules apply to the always-loaded and glob-scoped rule files of an agent runtime, such as `.claude/rules`, `.cursor/rules` or `.github/instructions`.

## General rule files

A general rule file is shipped outside a repository (user-level rules, or a rule package), and it applies to many repositories.

- Name a runtime-only mechanism (*e.g.* a skill, plan mode) only next to a neutral fallback, since the file reaches every runtime.
- Refer to another rule file by its role ("the language rule files"), never by filename, since each runtime installs it under another name.
- Record a task-specific exception in the rule it relaxes.

## Frontmatter

- Copy the frontmatter keys of a sibling, since each runtime reads its own (*e.g.* `applyTo`, `globs`, `paths`, `trigger`).
- When the file carries keys for several runtimes, give the glob keys the same value in each.
- On a rule that must always load, omit the glob keys and keep the always-on key of a sibling (*e.g.* `alwaysApply`, `trigger: always_on`).

## Placement

- A behavior for every task goes in the always-loaded rule.
- A convention for one kind of file goes in a glob-scoped rule file, so it loads only when that file is touched.
- A procedure for one kind of task goes in a skill rather than in an always-loaded rule.

## Size

Check each section of an always-loaded rule instead of counting lines.

- A section that applies to every task stays.
- A section that applies to one kind of task (*e.g.* releases, one subtree, one language) moves to a glob-scoped rule or a skill.
- Propose each move in the report, and apply it only once the user agrees.
